result.rationale: In updateEvent the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the comparison matches nothing and returns undefined where the old code returned `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` — the event update would target no specific calendar. In deleteEvent the same expression evaluates to undefined, causing `calendarId` to be undefined and the API to delete from 'primary' rather than the destination calendar. The mechanism is verifiable directly in the diff lines at packages/app-store/google

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 253-255 in the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts updateEvent method: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` - When externalCalendarId is falsy (null/undefined), the code falls through to the else branch which searches for a calendar where `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., where externalId equals null/undefined). This will never find a match, so selectedCalendar becomes undefined. The same bug exists in deleteEvent at line 314-316. This is a real logic error - the fallback condition is comparing against the very value that was already determined to be falsy.
